53851-deborah-a-tale-of-the-times-of-jud.title: Deborah A Tale Of The Times Of Judas Maccabaeus
53851-deborah-a-tale-of-the-times-of-jud.creator: James M. Ludlow
53851-deborah-a-tale-of-the-times-of-jud.description: A book by James M. Ludlow. King Antiochus, self-styled Epiphanes, the Glorious, was in a humor that ill-suited that title. He cursed his scribe who had just read to him a letter, kicked away the cushions where his royal and gouty feet had been resting, and strode about the chamber declaring that, by all the gods! he would make such a show in Antioch that the whole world would be agog with amazement.

arxiv-1909-05233.title: The Neural State Pushdown Automata
arxiv-1909-05233.creator: Ankur Mali aam35@psu.edu,, Alexander Ororbia ago@cs.rit.edu, C. Lee Giles clg20@psu.edu
arxiv-1909-05233.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Ankur Mali aam35@psu.edu,, Alexander Ororbia ago@cs.rit.edu, C. Lee Giles clg20@psu.edu. In order to learn complex grammars, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) require sufficient computational resources to ensure correct grammar recognition. A widely-used approach to expand model capacity would be to couple an RNN to an external memory stack. Here, we introduce a “neural state” pushdown automaton (NSPDA), which consists of a digital stack, instead of an analog one, that is coupled to a neural network state machine.

arxiv-2105-11794.title: Effects of interactivity and presentation on review-based explanations for recommendations
arxiv-2105-11794.creator: Diana C. Hernandez-Bocanegra, Jürgen Ziegler
arxiv-2105-11794.description: Abstract User reviews have become an important source for recommending and explaining products or services. Particularly, providing explanations based on user reviews may improve users’ perception of a recommender system (RS). However, little is known about how review-based explanations can be effectively and efficiently presented to users of RS.

arxiv-2108-13465.title: Full-Cycle Energy Consumption Benchmark for Low-Carbon Computer Vision
arxiv-2108-13465.creator: Xuanyi Dong Lu Liu Yuqing Yang Dongsheng Li
arxiv-2108-13465.description: Abstract The energy consumption of deep learning models is increasing at a breathtaking rate, which raises concerns due to potential negative effects on carbon neutrality in the context of global warming and climate change. With the progress of efficient deep learning techniques, e.g., model compression, researchers can obtain efficient models with fewer parameters and smaller latency.

arxiv-2109-13819.title: Perturbation theory for killed Markov processes and quasi-stationary distributions
arxiv-2109-13819.description: Abstract Motivated by recent developments of quasi-stationary Monte Carlo methods, we investigate the stability of quasi-stationary distributions of killed Markov processes under perturbations of the generator. We first consider a general bounded self-adjoint perturbation operator, and after that, study a particular unbounded perturbation corresponding to truncation of the killing rate.

arxiv-2207-12242.title: Multisymplectic Formulation of Deep Learning Using Mean–Field Type Control and Nonlinear Stability of Training Algorithm
arxiv-2207-12242.creator: Nader T. Ganaba
arxiv-2207-12242.description: Abstract As it stands, a robust mathematical framework to analyse and study various topics in deep learning is yet to come to the fore. Nonetheless, viewing deep learning as a dynamical system allows the use of established theories to investigate the behaviour of deep neural networks.

arxiv-2301-06855.title: Event-based Shape from Polarization
arxiv-2301-06855.creator: Manasi Muglikar, Leonard Bauersfeld, Diederik Paul Moeys, Davide Scaramuzza, [6pt] Robotics, Perception Group, University of Zurich, Switzerland
arxiv-2301-06855.description: Abstract State-of-the-art solutions for Shape-from-Polarization (SfP) suffer from a speed-resolution tradeoff: they either sacrifice the number of polarization angles measured or necessitate lengthy acquisition times due to framerate constraints, thus compromising either accuracy or latency. We tackle this tradeoff using event cameras.

arxiv-2306-10950.title: Benchmarking Robustness of Deep Reinforcement Learning approaches to Online Portfolio Management Thanks: This work benefited from the support of the Chair ”Artificial intelligence applied to credit card fraud detection and trading” led by CENTRALESUPELEC and sponsored by LUSIS. This work was perform
arxiv-2306-10950.creator: Marc Velay 1 , Bich-Liên Doan 1 , Arpad Rimmel 1 , Fabrice Popineau 1 and Fabrice Daniel 2
arxiv-2306-10950.description: Abstract Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) approaches to Online Portfolio Selection (OLPS) have grown in popularity in recent years. The sensitive nature of training Reinforcement Learning agents implies a need for extensive efforts in market representation, behavior objectives, and training processes, which have often been lacking in previous works.

arxiv-2308-10761.title: CoNe: Contrast Your Neighbours for Supervised Image Classification
arxiv-2308-10761.creator: Mingkai Zheng, Shan You, Lang Huang, Xiu Su, Fei Wang, Chen Qian, Xiaogang Wang, Chang Xu
arxiv-2308-10761.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mingkai Zheng, Shan You, Lang Huang, Xiu Su, Fei Wang, Chen Qian, Xiaogang Wang, Chang Xu. Image classification is a longstanding problem in computer vision and machine learning research. Most recent works ( e.g. 2020 , Triplet Schroff et al. 2015 , and max-margin Liu et al. 2016 ) mainly focus on grouping the intra-class samples aggressively and compactly, with the assumption that all intra-class samples should be pulled tightly towards their class centers.

arxiv-2309-03579.title: DTW+S: Shape-based Comparison of Time-series with Ordered Local Trends
arxiv-2309-03579.creator: Ajitesh Srivastava
arxiv-2309-03579.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ajitesh Srivastava. Measuring distance or similarity between time-series data is a fundamental aspect of many applications including classification and clustering. Existing measures may fail to capture similarities due to local trends (shapes) and may even produce misleading results. Our goal is to develop a measure that looks for similar trends occurring around similar times and is easily interpretable for researchers in applied domains.

arxiv-2502-19612.title: Evaluation of Hate Speech Detection using Large Language Models and Geographical Contextualization
arxiv-2502-19612.creator: Anwar Hossain, Monoshi Roy, Swarna Das
arxiv-2502-19612.description: Abstract The proliferation of hate speech on social media is one of the serious issues that is bringing huge impacts to society: an escalation of violence, discrimination, and social fragmentation. The problem of detecting hate speech is intrinsically multifaceted due to cultural, linguistic, and contextual complexities and adversarial manipulations.

arxiv-2508-18433.title: The Painlevé I hierarchy: Correspondence between the isomonodromic approach and the minimal models of the KP hierarchy
arxiv-2508-18433.creator: 1 Mohamad Alameddine , 2 Nathan Hayford , 3 Olivier Marchal
arxiv-2508-18433.description: Abstract Abstract : Two approaches to the Painlevé I hierarchy are discussed: the isomonodromic construction based on meromorphic connections, and the minimal models construction based on a reduction of the KP hierarchy. An explicit correspondence between both formalisms is built which gives the identification of these setups. In particular, this provides new expressions for the Lax matrices and Hamiltonians.

arxiv-2511-02410.title: Every group is represented by an incidence geometry
arxiv-2511-02410.creator: Antonio Díaz Ramos, Rémi Molinier, Antonio Viruel
arxiv-2511-02410.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Antonio Díaz Ramos, Rémi Molinier, Antonio Viruel. We investigate the relationship between finite groups and incidence geometries through their automorphism structures. Building upon classical results on the realizability of groups as automorphism groups of graphs, we develop a general framework to represent pairs of finite groups ( G , H ) (G,H) , where H ​ ⊴ ​ G H\trianglelefteq G , as pairs of correlation–automorphism groups of suitable incidence geometries.

arxiv-2602-16908.title: Multi-objective optimization and quantum hybridization of equivariant deep learning interatomic potentials on organic and inorganic compounds
arxiv-2602-16908.creator: G. Laskaris, D. Morozov, D. Tarpanov, A. Seth, J. Procelewska, G. Sai Gautam, A. Sagingalieva, R. Brasher, A. Melnikov
arxiv-2602-16908.description: Abstract Allegro is a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) model designed to predict atomic properties in molecules using E(3) equivariant neural networks. When training this model, there tends to be a trade-off between accuracy and inference time. For this reason we apply multi-objective hyperparameter optimization to the two objectives.

A change of perceived finger location towards the rubber hand (proprioceptive drift) has...

pmc-10562382.title: Sclerostin antibody improves alveolar bone quality in the Hyp mouse model of X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH)
pmc-10562382.creator: Kelsey A Carpenter, Delia O Alkhatib, Bryan A Dulion, Elizabeth Guirado, Shreya Patel, Yinghua Chen, Anne George, Ryan D Ross
pmc-10562382.description: X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) is a rare disease of elevated fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) production that leads to hypophosphatemia and impaired mineralization of bone and teeth. The clinical manifestations of XLH include a high prevalence of dental abscesses and periodontal disease, likely driven by poorly formed structures of the dentoalveolar complex, including the alveolar bone, cementum, dentin, and periodontal ligament.

pmc-11322411.title: GRK2 kinases in the primary cilium initiate SMOOTHENED-PKA signaling in the Hedgehog cascade
pmc-11322411.creator: Madison F. Walker, Jingyi Zhang, William Steiner, Pei-I Ku, Ju-Fen Zhu, Zachary Michaelson, Yu-Chen Yen, Annabel Lee, Alyssa B. Long, Mattie J. Casey, Abhishek Poddar, Isaac B. Nelson, Corvin D. Arveseth, Falko Nagel, Ryan Clough, Sarah LaPotin, Kristen M. Kwan, Stefan Schulz, Rodney A. Stewart, Joh
pmc-11322411.description: During Hedgehog (Hh) signal transduction in development and disease, the atypical G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) SMOOTHENED (SMO) communicates with GLI transcription factors by binding the protein kinase A catalytic subunit (PKA-C) and physically blocking its enzymatic activity. Here, we show that GPCR kinase 2 (GRK2) orchestrates this process during endogenous mouse and zebrafish Hh pathway activation in the primary cilium.

pmc-11355318.title: Germline RAD51C and RAD51D Mutations in High-Risk Chinese Breast and/or Ovarian Cancer Patients and Families
pmc-11355318.creator: Ava Kwong, Cecilia Yuen Sze Ho, Chun Hang Au, Sze Keong Tey, Edmond Shiu Kwan Ma, Manuela Ludovisi
pmc-11355318.description: Background: RAD51C and RAD51D are crucial in homologous recombination (HR) DNA repair. The prevalence of the RAD51C and RAD51D mutations in breast cancer varies across ethnic groups. Associations of RAD51C and RAD51D germline pathogenic variants (GPVs) with breast and ovarian cancer predisposition have been recently reported and are of interest.

pmc-11431454.title: Associations of Longitudinal Multiparametric MRI Findings and Clinical Outcomes in Intra-Articular Injections for Knee Osteoarthritis
pmc-11431454.creator: Woo Young Kang, Suk-Joo Hong, Ji-Hoon Bae, Zepa Yang, In Seong Kim, Ok Hee Woo, Georg Böning, Johannes Kahn
pmc-11431454.description: Background: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a complex disease marked by the degradation of articular cartilage. Objective: This study aimed to explore the relationship between cartilage volume/thickness and clinical outcomes in knee OA patients treated with intra-articular injections over one year. Methods: Twenty-four patients with mild-to-moderate OA were retrospectively analyzed using knee MRI.

pmc-11580552.title: Correlation between PDGF-BB and M1-type macrophage in inflammatory bowel disease: a case-control study
pmc-11580552.creator: Zhiyun Fang, Siwen Qu, Xia Ji, Chuwei Zheng, Juanfen Mo, Jianqiu Xu, Jinming Zhang, Haiyan Shen
pmc-11580552.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundInflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic disease in which macrophages play an important role in its pathogenesis. Platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB) secreted by macrophages is involved in the repair of vascular endothelial injury during inflammatory reactions.MethodsThe expression levels of M1 macrophages and PDGF-BB in serum and colonic mucosa of 30 patients with Crohn’s disease (CD) and 30 patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays and immunohistochemistry.

pmc-12505044.title: Oligogenic structure of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis has genetic testing, counselling and therapeutic implications
pmc-12505044.creator: Alfredo Iacoangeli, Allison A Dilliott, Ahmad Al Khleifat, Peter M Andersen, Nazlı A Başak, Johnathan Cooper-Knock, Philippe Corcia, Philippe Couratier, Mamede deCarvalho, Vivian E Drory, Jonathan D Glass, Marc Gotkine, Yosef M Lerner, Orla Hardiman, John E Landers, Russell L McLaughlin, Jesus S Mor
pmc-12505044.description: BackgroundDespite several studies suggesting a potential oligogenic risk model in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), case–control statistical evidence implicating oligogenicity with disease risk or clinical outcomes is limited. Considering its direct clinical and therapeutic implications, we aim to perform a large-scale robust investigation of oligogenicity in ALS risk and in the disease clinical course.

pmc-13097863.title: Ethical, legal, and social issues of AI use in emergency healthcare: a scoping review
pmc-13097863.creator: James Edgar Lim, Fahad Javaid Siddiqui, Angela Ballantyne, Michael Dunn, Sinead Prince, Dominic Wilkinson, Jonathan Lewis, Sungwon Yoon, Julian Savulescu, G. Owen Schaefer
pmc-13097863.description: BackgroundAdvances in artificial intelligence (AI) systems suggest that they can be used to improve healthcare outcomes via diagnosis, prognostication, patient management, risk assessment, etc. AI systems could be particularly useful in emergency healthcare (EHC) by synthesizing data to generate accurate conclusions rapidly. But the use of AI in EHC raises ethical, legal, and social concerns.

pmc-13171204.title: A Novel Approach to Map the Causal Impact of Brain Stimulation on Semantic Processing With Language Models
pmc-13171204.creator: Andrea Bruera, Gesa Hartwigsen
pmc-13171204.description: Noninvasive brain stimulation studies on semantic cognition hold the promise of revealing the functional relevance of brain areas through causal intervention. A primary challenge, however, is that findings are often interpreted through binary distinctions between sets of stimuli (e.g., related/unrelated words, same/different semantic category).

pmc-13465358.title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis suggests a potential regulatory network underlying leaf color transition in Ulmus pumila ‘Jinye’
pmc-13465358.creator: Yanan Jing, Yaoqian Yang, Yamei Hu, Fuxia Bo, Songhua Dai, Shufang Yan, Shuxiang Feng, Guojun Zhang
pmc-13465358.description: BackgroundUlmus pumila ‘Jinye’ is valued for its bright golden leaves, but this coloration is unstable during development, leading to a “regreening” phenomenon that reduces its ornamental value. Understanding the molecular mechanism underlying this transition is essential for stabilizing the golden leaf phenotype.
